fieldNotes.siteResolution: The audit target was given as 'US PL Cabazon Factory' / Arrowhead Cabazon bottling plant at 14020 Elm St, Cabazon CA, coords 33.9164,-116.7873. Those coords + that street address are the corporate/mailing address of record (D&B, BuzzFile, Yelp, Manta all list 14020 Elm St) and land on a small fenced warehouse cluster on the south frontage road of I-10. Street View there revealed the east gated building is the COUNTY OF RIVERSIDE - CABAZON - FLEET SERVICES, not Arrowhead. Web research (Nestle/PRNewswire/Foundation Windpower) established the actual operating plant is the 390,000 sqft Nestle/BlueTriton/Primo Arrowhead bottling plant on the Morongo Band of Mission Indians reservation along I-10, identifiable by its three on-site GE wind turbines (first on-site wind turbines at any Nestle plant; ~1 billion bottles/yr). Satellite resolved that plant at 33.9133,-116.7517, ~1.6km ESE of the mailing address. Two wind turbines + their long shadows, a substation, and water-storage tanks at the SW corner positively confirm it. The audit is of this real operating plant, not the Elm St mailing-address warehouse.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One very large bottling-plant/warehouse building (the ~390k sqft main structure, long axis running NW-SE) plus a separate long single-story admin/maintenance building at the SW corner; minor utility structures (substation, water tanks, turbine pads) counted with the complex. buildingCount=2.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm, sliding gate, or staffed booth visible across the truck approach. The site sits in open desert on tribal land; a single paved access road climbs ~600m from the SW (off the Apache Trail / Seminole Dr area) and opens directly onto the paved yard. Street View from the access road (pano XV-fnhv-vjC6iaPUPaq7sw, Dec 2025, looking E/NE at the plant) shows a wide open paved entrance with no gate, arm, or guard structure. Marked false, MEDIUM confidence: the nearest Street View pano stops ~150-200m short of the building, so a gate at the very edge of the paved yard cannot be 100% excluded from imagery; overhead z19-z20 of the entrance pinch show no booth or arm.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No 1-3-vehicle-footprint booth with multi-side windows at the entrance or anywhere along the approach. The only small structures are the SW admin/maintenance building (too large, set back from any gate) and utility sheds by the substation. False.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because no truck gate is confirmed (remoteGs requires a gate present but unstaffed).
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Continuous dock-door bank runs the entire NE/E face of the main building (the building's long NE wall), with trailers backed in along its full length across z18 (NE) and z19 (mid-dock) crops. Honest count of bays across the whole face is ~55-60; banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Enormous paved trailer drop yard fills the NE/E and SE of the property: multiple long rows of 53' trailers parked without tractors, plus tractor-trailer combos. ~40+ trailers visible in the single z19 mid-yard tile and many more across the NE z18 tile. Banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropYard: True - a dedicated, marked multi-row trailer-storage lot occupies the eastern half of the paved yard, distinct from the active dock apron.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Counted across z17/z18 (NE corner) + z19 (mid-dock) + z20 tiles: roughly 30-40 backed at the dock face and 50-60 parked in the drop-yard rows; total estimate ~95. Mixed imagery exposure (overexposed white roof bleeds into the dock edge) makes this approximate.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: The marked drop-yard rows plus the wide drive aisles and apron could hold ~120-130 trailers at practical capacity; estimate 130.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved internal yard between the dock apron and the drop-yard rows acts as a queue/maneuvering/staging area inside the property. True.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The ~600m private access drive plus the deep internal paved yard easily hold 3+ trucks queued before the docks. True.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Abundant unused paved width at the open entrance and broad internal aisles - ample physical room to add a bypass/express check-in lane. True (the site is wide open, not lane-constrained).
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: A single access road serves the property (one road in from the SW), so entry and exit share the same point. entryExitTogether=true; entryLanes/exitLanes ~1 each at the road, MEDIUM confidence (the open paved mouth could be driven as multiple lanes).
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: The dock doors read as one long continuous bank on a single building face (NE), not two physically separate clusters - so shipRcvSeparate marked false. MEDIUM confidence: a 390k sqft bottling plant likely segregates inbound packaging/raw vs outbound finished internally, but that function is not distinguishable from imagery.
fieldNotes.scale: No clearly identifiable truck-scale pad + scale house resolved at the entrance or in the yard; a desert dirt patch near the entrance is ambiguous. Marked false, listed uncertain.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Isolated 390k sqft plant in open Sonoran/Colorado desert on the Morongo reservation, set well back from the small town of Cabazon and the I-10 frontage. Rural.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Remote desert location away from dense development; cellular coverage likely adequate near the I-10 corridor but the site is isolated. Inferred true, MEDIUM confidence - listed uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property; nearest rail is the BNSF mainline well south, not connected. False.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~38 acres of building + paved yard inside the operational footprint, derived from the perimeter polygon; the leased reservation parcel is larger but is open desert, not yard.
fieldNotes.windTurbines: Two GE wind turbines are visible on-site (SW corner pads + long blade shadows); press records cite three turbines total supplying ~50% of plant electricity. Not a yard-classification field but a positive ID landmark.
fieldNotes.imageryQuality: Maxar/Airbus tiles; the white plant roof is overexposed and bleeds into the NE dock edge at z20, so the exact dock-door count is read better from z18/z19. Street View exists only on the public access road approaching from the SW (Dec 2025), stopping short of the property edge - no in-yard panos.
